name: Bhadresh Shah
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun India (2015-2019)
forbes_bio: Bhadresh Shah founded and runs AIA Engineering, a niche metallurgical company in Ahmedabad city.
Shah started a small foundry in 1978 and parlayed it into a $540 million (revenue) company.
AIA is the world's second largest manufacturer of high chromium grinding parts (by sales) for the cement, mining and power industries.
Shah is a metallurgy engineer from the premier Indian Institute of Technology (Kanpur).
Shah also sits on the Board of Zydus Lifesciences, controlled by pharma billionaire Pankaj Patel.
forbes_facts: Shah hails from a family of doctors but chose to study engineering rather than medicine.

name: Pan Dong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026); Hurun Self-Made Women (2021-2025)
forbes_bio: Pan chairs the Blue Moon Group, a supplier of liquid detergent and soap.
Pan is the wife the Blue Moon's founder and CEO Luo Qiuping.
Pan was a technical consultant until her formal appointment as Blue Moon's chief technology officer in 2003.
Blue Moon was founded in the southern Chinese city of Guangzhou in 1994.

name: Duncan MacMillan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Duncan MacMillan cofounded financial data and media company Bloomberg LP in 1981 with Mike Bloomberg, Thomas Secunda and Charles Zegar.
MacMillan left a job at investment bank Salomon Brothers to help Bloomberg with what was then called Innovative Market Systems.
He is credited with designing many of Bloomberg LP's computer systems.
Bloomberg LP has estimated revenues of nearly $15 billion.
forbes_facts: An active philanthropist, MacMillan has signed the Giving Pledge, a promise to give at least half of his fortune to charitable causes.
MacMillan served four years in the Marine Corps after graduating from high school. He graduated from Rutgers University in 1966.

name: Zhang Baoquan
appears_on: Hurun Global (2016-2022); Hurun China (2008-2021); Hurun Self-Made Women (2017-2019)

name: Nelson Peltz
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2005-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Nelson Peltz, an activist investor, is a founder of investment firm Trian Fund Management.
Trian now has $8.5 billion in assets under management.
The firm has a highly concentrated portfolio that includes stakes in Bank of New York Mellon, DuPont and food conglomerate Mondelez International.
In early 2017, Peltz battled with Proctor & Gamble over a board seat the company didn't want to grant him. He ultimately won the seat.
Peltz's daughter, Nicola, married Brooklyn Beckham, son of soccer player David Beckham, in April 2022 at the family's mansion in Palm Beach, Florida.

name: Matt Hulsizer
forbes_bio: Matt Hulsizer cofounded options trading firm Peak6 Capital Management in 1997 with his now-wife Jenny Just.
The duo have launched or bought about 15 companies through the investment firm, Peak6.
Hulsizer's fortune comes from Apex Fintech Solutions, which handles backend trading and technology for fintechs such as SoFi, Ally, eToro and WeBull.
Apex Fintech Solutions canceled plans to go public via a SPAC merger in December 2021; the deal would have valued the company at $4.7 billion.

name: Chen Jingye
appears_on: Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun China (2020-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2021); Hurun China U40 (2020-2021)

name: Patricia Angelini Rossi
name_chinese: 帕特里夏·安吉丽尼·罗西
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Patricia Angelini Rossi inherited a stake in Grupo Empresas Angelini, the Chilean investment group headed by her brother, Roberto Angelini Rossi.
The group's largest holding is publicly-traded Antarchile, which distributes fuel, operates fishing and shipping businesses and invests in energy.
Antarchile's forestry subsidiary, Arauco, entered North America in 2012 with the purchase of Canada's Flakeboard, which manufactures wood panels.
The group was previously headed by Patricia's uncle, Anacleto Angelini, who died in 2007.

name: Ilyas Khan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2025)
forbes_bio: Ilyas Khan founded quantum computing startup Quantinuum.
Khan was born in the United Kingdom and started his career at British investment bank Schroders before relocating to Hong Kong and working with Citi Group and Nomura.
He later ran Asia-focused tech accelerator Tech Pacific and took it public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2000.

Khan credits a conversation with the British physicist Stephen Hawking with inspiring him to start quantum software startup Cambridge Quantum in 2014, which he merged with Honeywell's trapped ion computer unit in 2021.
Honeywell took Quantinuum public on the Nasdaq in June 2026. Khan owns around 15% of its stock and is the Chief Product Officer and Vice-Chairman of the company.
forbes_facts: Khan served as the inaugural chairman of Stephen Hawking's foundation until 2018.
Khan is the former owner of English Football League team Accrington Stanley.

name: Lalit Keshre
forbes_bio: Lalit Keshre created investment app Groww along with three former colleagues in 2016. Four years later it became a unicorn.
The four cofounders were previously working at Indian e-commerce outfit Flipkart.
Bengaluru-based Groww has more than 50 million customers and two-thirds of them are under 35.
The company's IPO in November 2025 raised $83 million and made Keshre a billionaire.
forbes_facts: Keshre was born in a farming family in Lepa, a remote village in Madhya Pradesh state.
A graduate of the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, he started his career as a product manager at Flipkart.

name: Neerja Sethi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun India (2018-2022)
forbes_bio: Neerja Sethi cofounded IT consulting and outsourcing firm Syntel with her husband Bharat Desai in 1980 and took it public in 1997.
French IT firm Atos SE bought Syntel for $3.4 billion in 2018. Sethi got an estimated $510 million for her stake.
Sethi served as an executive at Syntel from its founding until its sale in 2018.
Her husband Bharat Desai is also a billionaire; they met in the U.S. while working for IT firm Tata Consultancy Services.
The couple started Syntel in their apartment in Troy, Michigan with an initial investment of just $2,000.
forbes_facts: Sethi holds an undergraduate degree in mathematics and a masters degree in computer science.
She and her husband joined the Giving Pledge, a commitment to give at least half their fortune to charitable causes, in May 2025.
